This is the only monitor in the set that watches something a USER sees. Every
other one watches whether our own work happened; a JS error breaks the page in
front of somebody while every server-side signal stays green.
A count and not a rate, unlike the APM row, because RUM sessions are the
denominator and they swing by an order of magnitude between an Indian evening
and 04:00 IST. A 1%-of-sessions threshold would be one error at night. 20 in
15 minutes is a floor under the noise of a single unlucky browser and still
catches a bad deploy inside one evaluation.

name: [{{env}}] stockbook-web — more than 20 browser errors in 15 minutes
message:
stockbook-web raised more than 20 RUM errors in 15 minutes.

RUM Explorer: `@type:error service:stockbook-web env:{{env}}`, group by `@error.message`, then by `@view.url_path`. One message across many paths is a shared component or a bad deploy; many messages on one path is that page.

`@context.boundary` is present on errors reported from a React error boundary (`error` or `global-error`). A `global-error` one is the more serious: it escaped the root layout, so the app shell itself failed to render.

@{{notify}}
_notify_no_data_rationale: FALSE. Zero browser errors is the goal, and overnight IST there are barely
any SESSIONS, let alone errors. Paging on that would mute the channel.
'RUM stopped reporting entirely' is a real failure — a broken client token, a
bad deploy dropping the provider — and it is NOT covered here. It is a
session-volume question and belongs on the web-vitals board (MONEY-1361),
